notes: Census figures for each geography come from the 2021 Census Profile (Statistics Canada catalogue 98-316-X2021001). The values were pulled programmatically from the Census Profile SDMX API (https://api.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/profile/sdmx/rest/data/STC_CP,DF_CSD/A5.<DGUID>.1.. and DF_CMACA for CMAs) because the www12 HTML pages sit behind a bot challenge. The source_url fields point to the human-readable profile pages for the same DGUIDs: Kelowna CY 2021A00055935010, Kelowna CMA 2021S0503915, West Kelowna CY 2021A00055935029, Kamloops CY 2021A00055933042, Kamloops CMA 2021S0503925.

Census counts are randomly rounded to multiples of 5. Immigration, ethnicity, visible minority, Indigenous identity, industry, tenure and mobility use 25% sample data; age and language use 100% data. Census day was May 11, 2021, during COVID-19, so 2020 incomes include pandemic benefits and the census unemployment rate is not comparable with the LFS.
Shares aged 15-24 are derived by summing the 15-19 and 20-24 counts and dividing by the age-group total; they are not published directly.

Census median ages and the July 1, 2025 estimate medians differ partly because of method: estimates adjust for census net undercoverage, which is concentrated among young adults. Do not read the drop from 44.4 (2021 census) to 42.3 (2025 estimate) in the Kelowna CMA as purely real ageing or rejuvenation.

Census NPR counts (Kelowna CY 3,950) are known undercounts and predate the 2022-2024 temporary-resident surge. StatCan publishes current NPR stock only nationally and provincially; at CMA level only annual net NPR flows are available (Table 17-10-0149-01). These show net NPR inflows collapsing in 2024/25: Kelowna CMA +222, Kamloops CMA -372.

Language lists use single responses only. 'English and non-official language(s)' (Kelowna CY: 2,325 mother tongue, 2,395 most often at home) is a multiple-response category and was excluded from the rankings.

CMHC Rental Market Survey figures cover purpose-built private rental apartments in structures with 3+ units (October survey). They exclude secondary-market rentals (rented condos, basement suites), which make up a large part of Kelowna's rental supply; the 2025 rental-condo table for Kelowna is suppressed. Kelowna CMA has only two survey zones (Core Area, Rutland). The latest survey available as of Oct 3, 2026 is October 2025 (released Dec 2025); the October 2026 survey will be released around Dec 2026.

LFS CMA unemployment rates are 3-month moving averages, seasonally adjusted, with large sampling error for small CMAs. Kelowna ranged from 4.4% to 10.4% and Kamloops from 3.8% to 9.8% within 12 months. Present a range or trend rather than a single month. September 2026 LFS data is due Oct 9, 2026. The annual-average CMA table (14-10-0385-01) is inactive.

TFW data (ESDC) are positions on positive LMIAs, which are approvals rather than arrivals, and are published only by economic region. Thompson-Okanagan (5930) covers Kamloops and the whole Okanagan/Shuswap, so it cannot be attributed to Kelowna or Kamloops. The quarterly pattern (Q4 + Q1 = 70% of 2025 primary-agriculture positions) reflects approvals ahead of the spring-to-fall growing season.

COEDC tourism figures (2.12M overnight trips, $2.4B output) are published by an official regional body but probably derive from Tourism Kelowna research and are not footnoted. Label them as regional economic development figures.

kelowna.ca and ylw.kelowna.ca block automated fetches (HTTP 403). The YLW monthly passenger table and the City of Kelowna city-profile and annual-report pages were read through a browser on Oct 3, 2026.

BC comparators (2021 census): immigrants 29.0%, NPR 3.5%, visible minority 34.4%, Indigenous 5.9%, median age 42.8, 65+ 20.3%, median household income $85,000. Kelowna and Kamloops are both far less diverse than BC overall, which is dominated by Metro Vancouver.

NOT FOUND officially: (1) a ranked list of COEDC/Central Okanagan major employers. Checked: the COEDC 2025 Economic Profile PDF, the Industry and Economic Profiles page, all COEDC sector pages, an investkelowna.com site search for 'major employers', and kelowna.ca economic development, city profile and annual report pages (the 2025 report is on Issuu and not text-searchable); web searches only turned up real-estate blogs. (2) Okanagan College Kelowna-campus enrolment and international share: the IAPR 2024-25 and data pages are college-wide only. (3) CMA- or city-level temporary foreign worker counts: only ESDC economic-region LMIA positions exist, and IRCC open data has no TFWP/IMP-by-CMA file except PGWP. (4) Current NPR stock by CMA. (5) An official monthly visitor or hotel-occupancy seasonality series for Kelowna (YLW passengers used as a proxy). (6) A 2025 annual-average LFS unemployment rate by CMA. (7) A CMHC West Kelowna rent or vacancy figure.
